Name: uav_lowlight_t4_smoke
Title: Low-light aerial small-object detection: synthetic pipeline smoke test
Short Hypothesis: Low-light degradation can reduce small-object detection recall; this tiny experiment checks execution and measurement, not statistical significance or novelty.
Related Work: No literature search or novelty claim is required for this infrastructure smoke test.
Abstract: SMOKE TEST ONLY. Generate synthetic aerial-style RGB images locally: 128 training, 32 validation and 32 held-out test images, each 128x128, with one to three non-overlapping 4-12 pixel vehicle-like rectangles and known bounding boxes on textured backgrounds. These are procedural proxies, NOT real UAV imagery or a benchmark dataset. Use fixed disjoint splits and paired clean/dark versions of held-out scenes. Darken by multiplying intensity by 0.2 and adding small seeded sensor noise; clamp to [0,1]. Train exactly one tiny convolutional grid detector with objectness and bounding-box regression, fewer than one million parameters, for at most two epochs with batch size 8. Assign at most one object per grid cell when generating scenes. Use PyTorch already installed on Colab; no downloads, pretrained weights, new dependencies, hyperparameter search, extra datasets or architecture variants. Require torch.cuda.is_available() and assert that model parameters and training tensors are on CUDA; never silently fall back to CPU. Print GPU name, torch version, training duration and peak allocated GPU memory. Finish the entire script in under five minutes on a T4. Evaluate the same trained detector on paired clean and low-light test images with one-to-one bounding-box matching at IoU >= 0.5, fixed confidence threshold 0.25 and NMS; report precision and recall with correct empty-prediction handling. Do not call these metrics mAP. Zero recall is acceptable for this smoke test and must not trigger longer training. Save finite losses, metrics, split seeds, runtime, GPU metadata and detector settings using the harness experiment_data.npy schema, plus a loss curve and a small labeled prediction montage. Do not save large checkpoints. Never fabricate metrics or claim low-light robustness from this tiny synthetic experiment. CPU-only local plotting must work from saved arrays without loading torch or requiring a GPU. Stage-one implementation only; the harness may perform one additional seed evaluation under the same limits. REQUIRED IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS: training must contain exactly 64 clean and 64 low-light samples, record both counts and assert them. Store torch.__version__ only as str(torch.__version__), never as PyTorch's custom TorchVersion object. Read the model/training seed from os.environ.get('AUTORESEARCH_SEED', '42'); keep split seeds fixed across repeats. Save only four paired example images for plotting, as uint8 arrays, rather than entire image datasets; keep experiment_data.npy below 1 MB. Metric parsing and plotting run locally without torch: use only numpy, matplotlib and the standard library.
Experiments: Train one tiny detector for two epochs on synthetic scenes with a fixed mixture of clean and degraded training examples.
Evaluate paired clean and dark test scenes; retain negative and zero-recall results.
Verify remote CUDA training, artifact synchronization, metric extraction, plotting and visual review.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Synthetic rectangles are not representative of real UAV targets or real nighttime imaging.
Two epochs and one repeat cannot establish detector quality or statistical significance.
This smoke test excludes literature search, later research stages and manuscript generation.
